item.title: Sanwo-Olu Gives Lagos Residents December 31 Deadline To Obtain Health Insurance - Health
item.description:

The governor announced the deadline on Tuesday during the launch of the enforcement programme under Executive Order EO/BOS/01 of 2024 in Victoria Island, Lagos.

At the event, Sanwo-Olu also unveiled the Lagos Private Health Plans (LPHP), a new initiative designed to provide...
item.content:encoded:
Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has directed residents to obtain health insurance on or before December 31, 2026, warning that enforcement of the policy will commence on January 1, 2027.

The governor announced the deadline on Tuesday during the launch of the enforcement programme under Executive Order EO/BOS/01 of 2024 in Victoria Island, Lagos.

At the event, Sanwo-Olu also unveiled the Lagos Private Health Plans (LPHP), a new initiative designed to provide health insurance coverage for salaried workers and corporate organisations across the state.

According to a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Gboyega Akosile, the policy requires residents, employers and employees in Lagos to obtain health insurance.

Sanwo-Olu explained that the initiative was aimed at ensuring residents could access quality healthcare without suffering financial hardship.

He noted that the existing Ilera Eko health insurance scheme primarily serves vulnerable residents and people working in the informal sector, while the newly introduced private health plans would cater to salaried workers and corporate organisations.

The governor urged employers to prioritise the health and welfare of their workers by providing health insurance, just as they make provisions for pensions and other employment benefits.

He also directed healthcare providers across Lagos State not to reject patients requiring emergency treatment because they could not immediately afford medical bills.

According to him, emergency patients must first receive the necessary treatment to stabilise their conditions before discussions about payment or insurance coverage begin.

Sanwo-Olu further disclosed that 21 Health Maintenance Organisations (HMOs) had agreed to participate in the new private health insurance plans.


He also appealed to Nigerian healthcare professionals considering leaving the country to reconsider their decisions, expressing optimism that improvements in healthcare financing would create better opportunities for practitioners.

Speaking at the event, Lagos State Commissioner for Health, Akin Abayomi, said the increasing cost of medical technology, equipment and treatment had placed a growing financial burden on patients.

Abayomi explained that expanding health insurance coverage would reduce the amount residents pay directly from their pockets when seeking medical attention.

He added that the initiative would also establish a more sustainable financing system for healthcare delivery across the state.

Meanwhile, Chairman of the Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA), Adebayo Adedewe, disclosed that the state government had increased its Health Equity Fund from ₦1 billion to ₦3 billion.

According to him, the fund would support health insurance coverage for more than 500,000 residents who cannot afford the required premiums.

Adedewe said LASHMA had also intensified public awareness campaigns to encourage residents to enrol in health insurance schemes.

He explained that the agency was using radio programmes, billboards and digital platforms to educate the public about the benefits of health insurance.

The agency is also collaborating with traditional rulers, market associations and transport unions to reach more residents and encourage them to register.

As part of efforts to strengthen the implementation of the programme, Sanwo-Olu inaugurated two boards during the event to support the administration and enforcement of the state’s health insurance policy.

Government officials, healthcare professionals and representatives of public and private organisations attended the launch.

The Lagos State Government is expected to begin enforcing the compulsory health insurance policy on January 1, 2027, following the December 31, 2026, deadline for residents to obtain coverage.

item.content:encoded:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yJPhs_HPgNc

A Nigerian man has accused the University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital (UPTH) of allegedly denying his brother emergency medical attention after they arrived at the hospital at about 2 a.m.

According to the man, he took his brother to the hospital's emergency ward, hoping he would receive urgent medical care. However, he claimed that hospital staff told them there was no blood pressure monitor available to check his brother's blood pressure.

He further alleged that they were asked to return at daybreak instead of receiving immediate attention.

The account has raised concerns about the availability of essential medical equipment and the provision of emergency healthcare, particularly during the early hours of the morning.

However, the circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear. The patient's medical condition, the nature of the emergency, and the hospital's account of the encounter have not been established from the information available.

UPTH's response would be important in clarifying the allegation and determining what occurred during the reported visit.

The incident has renewed attention to the importance of adequately equipped emergency departments and timely medical assessment for patients seeking urgent care.

item.content:encoded:
Former Vice President and ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has described the Federal Government’s ₦70,000 monthly transport support for public service workers as a desperate last minute attempt to contain public anger.

He said it admits that government policies have made life unbearable for millions.

In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said: “The Tinubu administration is scrambling from one announcement to another, showing its failure to grasp the crisis. The cost of living crisis reaches beyond transport: energy, food, rent and other essentials affect every part of daily life.

“Barbers pay more to power their clippers; restaurant owners face higher cooking costs; shopkeepers struggle to keep prices down; school bus operators pay more for fuel; and families still must buy food. Every business and household is affected. Does hardship end at the bus stop?

“If public service workers receive ₦70,000 monthly for transport from November, what happens to private sector workers, traders, small businesses, transport operators and millions without formal jobs? The public workforce is only a fraction of Nigeria’s population. A temporary allowance for some cannot solve a national crisis.

“The agreement also leaves the effective date for a new minimum wage unresolved. The government must publish payment dates, explain eligibility and say when wage negotiations will produce a decision.

“Any genuine relief is welcome, but a six month allowance cannot undo this hardship. At about ₦1,400 per litre, ₦70,000 buys roughly 50 litres of petrol. What meaningful difference can 50 litres make over an entire month?

“What Nigerians are witnessing is a government that set the house ablaze with its reckless policies, then pretends to fight the inferno by throwing ice cubes at the flames. A temporary ₦70,000 allowance cannot extinguish a cost of living crisis this government ignited.

“This is the pattern: the fuel discount failed, the 90 day cost of living plan failed before it began, and now comes another temporary payment. The government promised CNG would lower transport costs, but that promise has failed. For Nigerians still paying more to commute, the CNG programme is another scam of promises, while families face the same unaffordable prices.

“These rushed announcements smack of political bribery and corruption. Tinubu has shown no genuine intention of clearing the monumental mess caused by his hasty subsidy removal. He offers temporary payments instead of confronting the consequences.

“Atiku has proposed a practical alternative: a transparently managed production subsidy for fuel refined in Nigeria, delivering relief at the pump. Tinubu must not punish 250 million Nigerians for the corruption and leakages of a few thousand. His arrogance prevents him from reconsidering a cocky decision, while families and businesses pay the price.

“₦70,000 may help with transport, but it cannot explain why work, food and running a business have become unaffordable. Nigerians need lasting relief, decent wages and an economy that rewards honest work. When will life become affordable again?”

Atiku said his campaign would pursue practical measures to lower living costs, raise household incomes and restore dignity to work.

item.content:encoded:
Key Takeaways
-1). Five of the world’s 10 fastest-growing economies in 2027 are expected to be in the Middle East.
-2). Just three economies are projected to contract in 2027, compared with a global growth forecast of 3.4%.
-3). Five G7 economies rank among the world’s 20 slowest-growing, including Italy (0.6%), France (0.7%), Japan (0.7%), Germany (1.1%), and the UK (1.2%).

The Middle East is projected to lead global economic growth in 2027, as an anticipated recovery from the Iran war supports a rebound in energy production and exports. However, these forecasts depend on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returning toward prewar levels.

This graphic ranks the world’s fastest- and slowest-growing economies in 2027, based on real GDP growth projections from the IMF’s October 2026 World Economic Outlook.

Where Economic Growth Will Be Fastest in 2027
Iraq, Qatar, and Kuwait lead the global rankings, with each economy projected to grow by more than 17% in 2027.

These extraordinary growth forecasts follow steep projected contractions in 2026, including -16.0% in Iraq, -15.6% in Qatar, and -16.7% in Kuwait. The IMF assumes shipping through the Strait of Hormuz will gradually resume from March 2027, returning broadly to prewar conditions by October.

Outside the Middle East, Guyana ranks fourth at 16.8%, sustaining its rapid growth as offshore oil production expands. Vietnam (7.5%) and India (7.0%) are also among the fastest-growing economies, supported by manufacturing exports and domestic consumption, respectively.

Where Economic Growth Will Be Slowest in 2027
Bolivia (-1.5%), Equatorial Guinea (-1.0%), and Haiti (-0.5%) are the only economies projected to contract in 2027.

Several major advanced economies also appear near the bottom of the rankings. Italy, France, and Japan are all projected to expand by less than 1%, while Germany and the UK are forecast to grow by just 1.1% and 1.2%, respectively.

[i]Across Europe, elevated energy costs are weighing on consumption and industrial activity. Meanwhile, growing competition from Chinese exporters is expected to weigh on EU growth through 2028, as European manufacturers face increasing pressure in domestic and overseas markets.[/i]

Overall, euro area growth is projected at just 1.2% in 2027, compared with 2.3% in the United States. For European governments, the weak outlook comes as rising defense and infrastructure commitments place additional demands on already constrained public finances.

item.content:encoded:
BlackViper:
A 29 year-old man, Yusuf Ajisafe was on Wednesday docked in a Mapo Grade A Customary Court in Ibadan for allegedly beating up and inflicting injuries on his girlfriend who terminated their relationship.

Ajisafe pleaded not guilty to the three-count charge of malicious damage, assault and escape from lawful custody. The Prosecution Counsel, Insp Ayodele Ayeni told the court that the defendant committed the crime on Oct. 15, at about 4.30 p.m., at Idiaro area in Ibadan, Oyo State.

Ayeni stated that Ajisafe allegedly assaulted his girlfriend, Titiloye Balogun after she informed him that she was no longer interested in the relationship.

The police alleged that the defendant also inflicted injuries on Balogun using a sharp object and also destroyed goods in her shop worth N300,000.

Ayeni explained that Ajisafe escaped from police custody where he was being held, but was rearrested after an intense search.

He noted that the offence contravened the provisions of sections 451 and 249 of the criminal code cap 38 vol. ii laws of Oyo State of Nigeria 2000.

The court’s President, Mrs O.E. Owoseni, admitted the defendant to bail in the sum of N200,000 with two reliable sureties in like sum. Owoseni said that one of the sureties must be a relative. She adjourned the matter until Dec. 10 for trial.

item.title: Beyond The Mourning: The Deeper Issues Exposed By Toluwanisings’ Death - Celebrities
item.description:
The aftermath of the death of the famous gospel singer, Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, is beginning to follow a path similar to that of Mohbad. The reason is not far-fetched: money is involved. It does not have to be a large sum. As long as a few self-entitled people feel marginalised, there is bound to be a problem.

His wife has unknowingly inherited a problem that may never be fully resolved. The only reason there was a cold war rather than a full-blo...
item.content:encoded:
The aftermath of the death of the famous gospel singer, Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, is beginning to follow a path similar to that of Mohbad. The reason is not far-fetched: money is involved. It does not have to be a large sum. As long as a few self-entitled people feel marginalised, there is bound to be a problem.

His wife has unknowingly inherited a problem that may never be fully resolved. The only reason there was a cold war rather than a full-blown conflict was because the singer was still alive and the opposing parties remained hopeful. Now that he is gone, many of the financial promises he may have made can no longer be fulfilled. As a result, some people appear to be taking out their frustrations on his wife, and they may eventually extend that hostility to her children. If the widow were to spread a few million naira around, many of these critics would likely change their tune overnight.

I am concerned that a blogger who has exclusive access to vulnerable members of his family may be taking advantage of the situation. Social media users have criticised the blogger, but what should one expect? He saw an opportunity, it worked, his page is growing rapidly, and he is capitalising on what is bringing him attention. He interviews elderly members of the family, who freely share their views in a very raw and unfiltered manner.

The blogger has showcased the singer's father's unfinished house and highlighted how it reportedly remained unroofed despite promises that were made. A woman believed to be his aunt claimed she hardly received up to ₦10,000 from him. The standard of Toluwanisings' home appears to be in stark contrast to the conditions in which some of his family members live. It is almost like comparing Gaza to New York. Such a disparity naturally raises questions. While I am not in a position to tell anyone how to spend their hard-earned money, I do feel that the living conditions of some of his family members could have been better.

Collectivism and dependency have become a way of life in many African societies. It is one of the ways communities support one another. While this culture can sometimes become parasitic and detrimental, it remains deeply ingrained in our way of life. One of the worst assumptions a person can make is that they owe nobody anything. I rarely assume that all my money is mine alone. Although I am far from wealthy, I find fulfilment in keeping some extra cash available for close associates who genuinely need help. This is separate from the monthly support I give to my parents.

No matter how discreet you are about your achievements, people will make financial demands. Giving can be uncomfortable in Africa because the requests never seem to end. Contrary to what the Bible teaches, givers in a place like Nigeria are increasingly becoming broke due to over-giving. Returning to Toluwanisings' family situation, I believe an improvement in their circumstances, closer to his own standard of living, might have been beneficial. The living conditions of some family members do not appear remotely comparable to his. Of course, there may be much more to the story than the public currently knows.

The family reportedly wants him buried in his house, but his wife has allegedly objected. This is a very delicate issue. You cannot teach someone how to grieve. It is easy to tell a boxer to get up after a punch when you are merely watching from the side-lines. When life delivers a devastating blow, only then do you understand what survival mode truly feels like. The widow simply wants to heal and move forward for the sake of her wellbeing after losing a man she reportedly knew for more than 20 years, the father of her two children.

Again, life can feel fragile and fleeting. When someone dies, the world does not stop turning. Friends may mourn deeply and still share a cold drink later that day. Some may even return to their normal routines almost immediately. This is because nobody is indispensable. In the same vein, the widow is likely trying to find a way forward and rebuild her life. She has two children looking up to her. This is one of life's hardest realities to accept.

A report claimed that a visitor to the family's residence was surprised to find them eating takeaways rather than mourning. The visitor frowned upon it. However, life must go on. After all, would you start riding a horse simply because you were involved in a car accident and lost trust in automobiles?

Human behaviour is like an iceberg. What we see is only the tip. The underlying causes, often much larger and more significant, remain hidden beneath the surface. The actions of certain family members may stem from years of perceived neglect, and they appear to be directing those frustrations toward the widow. Some may even feel she took away their "cash cow."

One family member reportedly believes the singer's death was suspicious and has called for intervention from religious bodies, government institutions, and security agencies to uncover the truth behind his sudden and untimely passing. We have seen a similar situation before in the aftermath of Mohbad's death.

The widow is likely facing a long and emotionally exhausting journey. In a society where many people strongly believe in spiritual forces, she may fear that some family members harbour ill intentions toward her. Such fears can be deeply troubling, especially when the perceived threat exists largely in the mind.

The golden lesson from all of this is that when fortune smiles on us, we should do our best to improve the circumstances of our family members where possible. Procrastination can be a thief of time. If Toluwanisings' relatives had felt more included in his success, it is possible that many of the unpleasant revelations now emerging would have remained unsaid. Whether that would have been right or wrong is another debate entirely.

item.content:encoded:
Akpakomiza2:
It clearly shows tinubu is stronger than Atiku and will defeat him ruthlessly. Tinubu has presence in Adamawa and is fighting for votes here. What are Atiku's chances in lagos

As una dey support APC to continue, hunger jo dey tire una?

“By all means possible. Anyhow. I will give you electricity. If I fail, if you like, do not vote for me. A promise made, is a promise kept”.

Tinubu made thaf promise as part of his 2023 election campaign. So far in 2026, with three months to the next elections, electricity is worse. Has he kept the promise in Edo state? If he has, Okpebolo would not have complained against BEDC a few days ago.

Before 2023, Nigerians on the Buhari minimum wage of 30k fared better. Nigerians could purchase petrol for their generators when there was no FG electricity. Nowadays with the master strategist, Nigerians do not have FG electricity, neither can they afford to purchase petrol at 1,350 per liter.

Has BAT taken Nigerians forward? He met poverty at 56% under Buhari’s APC and presently he has taken it to 63% and counting, yet holds the opposition responsible. The opposition that he pushed out in 2015 with different promises of better life?

Should you be talking of “stronger” at this stage, or wishing the master strategist to relocate to France and relax, while someone better runs the country and returns sanity to the system?

Leaving Public Funds In The Bank Would Have Made Nigeria Very Wealthy- Peter Obi by omenka(op): 3:40pm
If Leaders Had Left Public Funds In Banks, Nigeria Would Be So Rich By Now That We Would Not Know What To Do With The Money — Peter Obi

The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has spoken about public funds, accountability and his record in education during a radio interview with Option FM in Akwanga, Nasarawa State, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

Speaking about money left in three different banks that generated interest, Obi said:

“I wish everybody in this country left money in the bank they have interest. Nigeria would have been so rich that we don’t know what to do with money.”

He further stated:

“In Nigeria, because it’s a criminalized place, the criminals will always come together to show what the honest person did. So in Nigeria, to be honest is to be a criminal. To be a criminal is to be honest.”

He added that if all Nigerian leaders had been leaving money in banks, the country would have accumulated so much wealth that it would not know what to do with it.

Speaking about his record as Anambra State governor, Obi said:

“I was the best in education, basic education as a governor. You can go and check the records. Oyeka Nweko is coming number one.”

He further stated that Professor Kole from Oxford University had visited Anambra State to witness the tremendous change in education.

Humanitarian Disaster, Disease Looms In North-west IDP Camps — Peacepro by experts(op): 2:39pm

Preventable Disease Outbreaks, Humanitarian Disaster Loom in North-West IDP Camps — PeacePro

More than 30 camps encountered in Sokoto; multiple settlements identified in Zamfara and Katsina as demands for relief intensify

The Foundation for Peace Professionals (PeacePro) has warned of looming disease risks and a worsening humanitarian crisis in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps across Nigeria’s North-West, calling for urgent intervention to provide food, safe drinking water, shelter, sanitation and healthcare to displaced families.

In a statement authorised by its Executive Director, Abdulrazaq Hamzat, PeacePro said field observations in Zamfara, Katsina and Sokoto States raised serious concerns about the welfare of displaced people, many of whom have reportedly established makeshift settlements after fleeing banditry with inadequate government support.

The organisation reported encountering more than 30 IDP camps during a visit to Sokoto State, including in the Sabon Birni area. In Zamfara, it identified settlements at Tsunami Camp, Government Secondary School Tsunami, Mareri, Tudun Wada and Unguwar Gwaza in Gusau, as well as camps in Anka, Lalan and Premier. It also raised concerns about displaced populations in Katsina State.

PeacePro warned that inadequate food, unsafe drinking water, poor shelter, deficient sanitation and limited access to healthcare could expose camp residents to preventable diseases and other serious health emergencies. It called for urgent medical assessments, disease surveillance, essential medicines and the immediate provision of basic relief supplies.

PeacePro linked the humanitarian crisis to the wider impact of banditry, which it says has forced residents to abandon more than 500 communities across the North-West. It stressed, however, that the immediate priority must be the survival and welfare of displaced people already living in camps.

PeacePro urged the Federal Government, the Zamfara, Katsina and Sokoto State Governments, emergency management agencies and humanitarian organisations to assess the camps urgently, identify underserved settlements and mobilise emergency assistance. It also called for transparent reporting on identified needs and the relief delivered.

Hamzat warned that the humanitarian consequences of insecurity must not be overlooked, stressing that people forced to flee violence should not be left without the basic necessities required to survive with dignity.

PeacePro called for a coordinated and sustained humanitarian response, alongside security measures that would enable displaced communities to return home safely when conditions permit.

item.title: 2027: ‘We’ll Rig Those Who Rig Elections,’ Peter Obi Talks Tough - Politics
item.description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has threatened to deal with those who rig elections in Nigeria, declaring that his administration would ensure electoral offenders face jail terms if he wins the 2027 presidential election.

Obi spoke on Wednesday at an NDC town hall meeting in Nasarawa State, where he addressed party supporters on electoral integrity and the need to strengthen Nigeria’s electoral system.

Responding to a qu...
item.content:encoded:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has threatened to deal with those who rig elections in Nigeria, declaring that his administration would ensure electoral offenders face jail terms if he wins the 2027 presidential election.

Obi spoke on Wednesday at an NDC town hall meeting in Nasarawa State, where he addressed party supporters on electoral integrity and the need to strengthen Nigeria’s electoral system.

Responding to a question about election rigging, the former Anambra State governor said the party would not allow electoral manipulation to go unchallenged in the next general election.

“You didn’t ask about what we are going to do if people rig election next year. Let me assure you, number one, this coming election, we will rig those who rig it,” Obi said.

He added that, if elected president, he would ensure that election rigging became impossible under his watch by strengthening political parties and reforming the electoral process.

“And let me assure you number two, if I’m elected the President of Nigeria, nobody will rig election in this country again because the first thing we need to do is to strengthen our parties, strengthen the process,” he said.

Obi also called for stricter laws governing eligibility to contest elections, arguing that candidates should be required to demonstrate that they had attended primary and secondary school.

“Our laws will be strict. For you to contest election, you must have attended a primary school, you must have attended a secondary school and it will be visible, it will be clear,” he said.

He warned that anyone who forged academic certificates or falsely claimed to possess the required qualifications would face imprisonment.

“If you didn’t attend any of them or forge your certificate, you go to jail,” Obi said.

The NDC candidate extended the warning to officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and others involved in election administration, saying anyone found guilty of rigging elections under his government would be prosecuted.

“Any INEC official, anybody who is involved with elections under my watch that rigs elections will go to jail,” he declared.

Obi said his proposed approach would be anchored on the rule of law, insisting that no individual, regardless of position, should be exempt from accountability.

“Under my watch, Nigeria must be a country that has a law, and both from the number one person to the last person must obey the rule of law,” he said.

“Nobody must be above the law; nobody will behave rascally.”

He said his political ambition was driven by a desire to change the country and build a system in which electoral rules were respected.

“That’s why we are doing what we are doing. We want to change Nigeria. A new Nigeria is possible, and that new Nigeria will be OK,” Obi added.

Putin Lectured Norway & Finland’s Leaders During Rare Phone Call (Photos) by WriterNig(op): 1:38pm*
🇳🇴 🇫🇮 📞 🇷🇺 Russian President Vladimir Putin delivered a lengthy lecture on medieval Slavic history to the leaders of Norway and Finland during an October 27 phone call, offering little mention of an immediate ceasefire despite renewed diplomatic efforts to end Moscow's war in Ukraine, the Financial Times reported.

[b]According to three sources familiar with the call between Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, and the Russian president, Putin spent most of the 90-minute call to deliver a lengthy rant about Russian historical fixations.

The call, which was initially planned to last half an hour, comes ahead of trilateral peace talks expected in the Emirati capital of Abu Dhabi sometime in November between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S.

Ukraine's calls for an immediate ceasefire were barely discussed during the phone call, the sources added. With one source telling FT that the leaders did not interrupt Putin's rant to gauge his seriousness on future dialogue with Europe.

Amid failed attempts at peace negotiations, Putin has repeatedly espoused his views on Russian history in conversations with world leaders. The Russian president reportedly gave a similar lecture to U.S. President Donald Trump during the August 2025 summit in Alaska, which reportedly included a lengthy lecture on medieval Rus princes, such as Rurik or Yaroslav the Wise, as well as the 17th-century Cossack leader Bohdan Khmelnytskyi.[/b]

🔗 Kyiv Independent | | Financial Times

Report: Current Govt Added More Debt in Two Years Than Nigeria Accumulated in 55 Years

• Decries Nigeria’s debt service-to-revenue ratio

•Urges FG to declare fiscal emergency

A new policy brief has warned that Nigeria’s worsening debt profile and weak revenue generation have pushed the country into a dangerous fiscal position, with the current administration accumulating more debt in two years than Nigeria recorded during its first 55 years after independence.

The report, released by the Alliance for Economic Research and Ethics LTD/GTE, a Nigerian policy think tank, argued that the country’s debt crisis has evolved into a governance and revenue emergency, as debt servicing obligations now exceed the federal government’s retained earnings.
>
>
According to the think tank, Nigeria’s public debt rose sharply from N87.38 trillion in June 2023 to N159.28 trillion by the end of 2025, with President Bola Tinubu’s administration accounting for about N65.9 trillion of the increase within its first two years in office.

The organisation in the brief titled: “Nigeria Is Borrowing to Breathe—and the Clock Is Ticking”, noted that Nigeria accumulated only about N12.06 trillion in debt from independence in 1960 up to 2015, meaning the current administration added more than five times that amount in just 24 months.

The report stated that while previous governments also contributed significantly to the country’s rising debt burden, the speed of accumulation under the current administration had intensified concerns over fiscal sustainability.

“President Bola Tinubu’s administration has added a further N65.9 trillion in just two years. To put that in perspective: it took Nigeria’s first 55 years of independence to accumulate N12 trillion in debt. The current administration has added more than five times that amount in 24 months,” it argued.

It recalled that Nigeria briefly became almost debt-free externally after the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo secured an $18 billion Paris Club debt relief package in 2005 and paid $12 billion to extinguish about $30 billion in external obligations.

Josep Gené during his visit to ...
item.content:encoded:
Spanish football executive Josep Gené Garcia has withdrawn from a proposed collaboration with Wikki Tourists FC, saying he received no formal response to his plans for the Bauchi-based club.

In a press statement sent directly to Yaro Insider on October 28, Gené said he had decided to end the proposed collaboration after efforts to obtain clarification about the professional arrangements and implementation plan yielded no clear response.

Josep Gené during his visit to Bauchi for the proposed Wikki Tourists FC collaboration.
Gené, founder and chairman of 2BPRO SPORTS, said he travelled from Spain to Bauchi following an invitation to contribute to the development of Wikki Tourists.

His proposed plan included developing young players, bringing Spanish coaches to work with Nigerian coaches, establishing international partnerships and generating revenue through professional player transfers.

He said the revenue would be reinvested in youth development, infrastructure and the club’s long-term future.

According to Gené, photographs of his visit were published on Wikki Tourists’ official social media pages on September 15, creating expectations among supporters and the wider football community.

However, he claimed that by October 27, he had received no formal response concerning his implementation plan or proposed professional agreements.

Gené said he had therefore decided to withdraw and asked that his name and image no longer be presented as representing an ongoing appointment or partnership with the club.

He also stressed that his decision was not directed at the Bauchi State Government. He thanked the governor, deputy governor, sports commissioner, club personnel and residents for their hospitality.

Gené said he remained open to discussions with the state government on broader sports development opportunities.

He praised Wikki Tourists supporters for their passion and expressed hope that the club would achieve promotion to the Nigeria Premier Football League.

Yaro Insider could not establish from the statement alone whether a formal agreement had been reached or why the proposed collaboration did not proceed. The club and the other individuals named in the statement should be given an opportunity to respond.

The development raises questions about the status of the proposed international partnership and whether the plan had progressed beyond initial discussions and public announcements.

Source: https://yaroinsider.ng/josep-gene-withdraws-wikki-tourists-deal/

Kaduna: ADC Guber Candidate, Isa Ashiru Blames El-Rufai For Insecurity by Akpakomiza2(op): 1:31pm
The Kaduna State gubernatorial candidate of the African Democratic Congress(ADC), Hon Isa Ashiru, has blamed the Malam Nasir El-Rufai’s administration for the escalation of insecurity in Kaduna State.

Speaking in an interview with Trust TV on Tuesday, Hon Ashiru attributed the insecurity in Kaduna State to retrenchment of many Traditional rulers by the previous administration, which has created a lot of ungoverned spaces.

‘’For instance, when the APC government came, they retrenched so many village heads and district heads. They left these places ungoverned. The report that is usually transmitted from the village head to district head head, to the Emir, for onward transmission to the Governor and Security Council meeting is no more,’’ he said.

It will be recalled that El-Rufai’s government had reverted to 77 districts and 1,429 village units that existed prior to 2001, effectively sacking the 313 district heads and 4,453 village heads appointed after the year 2001 by administration of former Governor Ahmed Mohammed Makarfi.

The then Governor had enacted the Traditional Institutions Law N0 21 of 2021 in June, which replaced the Chiefs (Appointment and Deposition) Law Cap 25 of 1991, to undertake sweeping controversial reforms to the traditional and emirate council system in Kaduna State.

In the interview with Trust TV, Hon Ashiru promised that his administration will bring the traditional rulers on board, so as to close the ungoverned spaces, pledging to provide operational vehicles for security agencies and give them incentives for putting their lives on the line.

The ADC candidate also said that his government will deploy the use of Artificial Intelligence ‘’because of the sophistication in the industry now,’’ adding that insecurity has become an industry because of the millions involved in the payment of ransom.

Decrying the security situation in the state, he expressed optimism that the matter will be reduced to the barest minimum, if not brought to an end, when his administration brings back the retrenched traditional rulers, deploys AI and gives incentives to security agencies, and provide them with operational vehicles.

Court Dismisses Emeka Ike’s ₦10 Billion Damages Suit Against Wike’s Aide, INEC by hisexcellency34(op): 12:10pm
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday dismissed N10 billion rights suit filed by the Nollywood actor Emeka Ike against Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant to FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Justice Salim Ibrahim, in a judgment, upheld the preliminary objections of the respondents on the grounds that the suit was incompetent and improperly constituted.

Court dismisses Emeka Ike’s N10bn damages suit against Wike’s aide, INEC.

Justice Ibrahim also dismissed the main suit on the ground of lack of proof.

The minister’s aide, through a post on X in May, was alleged to have mocked Ike by leaking his confidential voter registration details on social media.

The post was said to have shown details of Ike’s voter registration transfer from Imo to the nation’s capital.

Meanwhile, Ike, in the suit filed by L. T. Adeh, sued Olayinka and INEC as 1st and 2nd respondents in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1272/2026.

item.title: Before You Envy Anyone's Relationship Status, Read This - Romance
item.description:
If you are married, face your marriage. If you are single, take your time. Nothing dey street, and nothing dey marriage wey you should enter blindly.

Some singles see married people posting anniversary pictures, travelling with their spouses, raising children and enjoying companionship. They begin to wonder when their own turn will come.

Meanwhile, some married people see their single friends travelling without seeking permission, spending their money as they ple...
item.content:encoded:
If you are married, face your marriage. If you are single, take your time. Nothing dey street, and nothing dey marriage wey you should enter blindly.

Some singles see married people posting anniversary pictures, travelling with their spouses, raising children and enjoying companionship. They begin to wonder when their own turn will come.

Meanwhile, some married people see their single friends travelling without seeking permission, spending their money as they please, making personal decisions freely and enjoying a level of independence they no longer have. They begin to wonder whether marriage was worth it.

But there is something both sides often forget: you are comparing your private struggles with somebody else's public appearance.

That married couple posting beautiful pictures may be dealing with financial pressure, family interference, trust issues or problems they would never discuss on social media. That single person enjoying freedom may be battling loneliness, financial responsibilities or the frustration of not finding a suitable partner.

Marriage comes with companionship, shared responsibilities and the opportunity to build a family with someone you love. It also comes with sacrifices, compromises, financial obligations and the responsibility of considering another person's needs when making decisions.

Singlehood offers independence, flexibility and time to develop yourself. However, it can also come with loneliness, pressure from family and society, and uncertainty about finding the right person.

Neither situation is automatically better. Your experience depends largely on the choices you make and the circumstances you find yourself in.

The real problem is not being single or married. The problem is entering a situation you are not prepared for, or remaining in one that is destroying you simply because you are afraid of what people will say.

Don't marry because your friends are getting married, your parents are pressuring you or you are tired of attending weddings alone. Marriage is not a competition, and a wedding ceremony is not proof that someone has made the right choice.

Likewise, don't condemn marriage because you have seen people suffer in bad relationships. There are couples who genuinely enjoy their marriages, support each other's ambitions, resolve disagreements with maturity and build beautiful lives together.

If you are single, use the time to understand yourself, develop your character, improve your finances and learn what you need in a life partner. Don't just look for someone to marry. Look for someone with whom you can build a healthy life.

If you are married, stop romanticising the freedom of singlehood whenever marriage becomes difficult. Work on your relationship, communicate honestly and appreciate what you have, provided the relationship is safe and healthy.

Of course, this is not an argument for staying in an abusive or dangerous marriage. Protecting yourself matters more than maintaining appearances.

At the end of the day, marriage is not an automatic upgrade, and singlehood is not a life sentence. Both have advantages, disadvantages and responsibilities that people on the other side may not fully understand.

Stop envying what you see from a distance. Understand what you are choosing before you choose it.

My question is this: For those who are married If you could go back in time, would you still choose marriage or singlehood? And for those who have experienced both, which do you honestly find more fulfilling, and why?

17 Likes 1 Share

item.content:encoded:
No Justification For Fresh Borrowing Amid Revenue Gains — Senator Victor Umeh by dre11(op): 11:07am

…Says past loans failed to ease hardship

…2026 capital budget yet to be implemented

…Rising fuel prices show loans haven’t eased hardship

…No work on Eastern Rail Line despite $3bn loan approval

By Juliet Umeh

Senator Victor Umeh has questioned the Federal Government’s request for fresh loans, saying there is no justification for further borrowing when the government says it has surpassed its revenue targets.

Umeh, who represents Anambra Central, spoke on Channels Television’s programme, where he reacted to the President’s request for approval of additional external borrowing. He said the government should account for previous loans and show their impact on Nigerians’ lives.

“From what they have told us, there is no justification for the borrowing. Since you have surpassed your revenue expectations, there is no need taking the country into a circus around borrowing all the time,” he said.

Umeh said previous loans had been presented as funding for infrastructure, but Nigerians were yet to see the results.

“All the borrowing plans we have approved before have been hinged on the development of infrastructure. When you ask where the money is going, you are told the government needs money for emergencies,” he said.

He added: “What we want to see is how these monies you have borrowed have impacted positively on the lives of the Nigerian people.”
He said the country was in distress, with living costs rising while many people lacked money.
“The cost of living has become unacceptable. People don’t have money. They don’t have purchasing power in the midst of soaring costs,” he said.

Citing fuel prices, he said he had bought petrol at N1,410 per litre, while diesel was selling for about N1,889 per litre.

“When will these things come down? When can people buy petrol or diesel without complaints?” he asked.

Umeh criticised budget implementation, saying the 2026 capital budget had yet to be implemented as October drew to a close.
“In the 2026 budget, there is no implementation of the capital budget yet. This is the end of October. We have barely one month until the end of the year,” he said.
He cited a previously approved loan for the eastern rail line, saying no work was under way.

“Part of that $21 billion was $3 billion for the reconstruction of the Eastern Rail Line. No work is going on there,” he said.

He said the government should explain whether the funds had been accessed and how they had been used before seeking more loans.

Asked whether opposition lawmakers could block the request, Umeh said the governing majority had the numbers to secure its approval.

“We are not rubber stamps, but you don’t have the number to say no to it,” he said.

Re: No Justification For Fresh Borrowing Amid Revenue Gains — Senator Victor Umeh by nairalanda1(m): 11:28am

Why oil dependent countries borrow...with help of AI

If you like, laugh. I am laughing at you too..

Oil-dependent countries borrow too much because their national budgets and foreign currencies rely heavily on a single, volatile commodity.

Key Causes of Excessive Borrowing

• Price Volatility: Global oil prices swing wildly. When prices drop, government revenues crash, forcing countries to borrow to keep public services running.

• The "Paradox of Plenty": Abundant oil money often reduces the state's need to collect broad domestic taxes. Without a tax base, governments lack pressure from citizens to practice fiscal discipline.

• Rigid Spending Commitments: Governments build high public payrolls, social subsidies, and infrastructure around high oil prices. When oil prices fall, they cannot easily cut these costs, so they borrow to cover the gap.

• Weak Diversification and De-industrialization: High oil revenues can cause "Dutch disease"—where a strong currency makes local agriculture, technology, and manufacturing uncompetitive. This leaves the economy without alternative ways to generate income or jobs.

• Crude-Backed Loans and Forward Sales: Many oil producers mortgage their future production by taking advance cash loans tied to barrels of crude oil. For example, Punch Nigeria reports that forward crude sales by Nigeria's national oil company reached billions of dollars, eating up large shares of future daily output just to service debt.

• False Creditworthiness: High natural resource wealth can temporarily make a country look attractive to foreign lenders. Governments borrow heavily during boom times, only to face crushing repayment terms when the market turns

item.title: FG’s ₦70,000 Transport Allowance: 10 Things Public Servants Should Know - Politics
item.description:
The Federal Government has approved a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants for six months, beginning in November 2026, as part of measures to cushion the impact of rising living costs.

The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a conciliation meeting between the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress in Abuja on October 27, 2026.

The agreement also covers outstanding allowances, health workers’ arrears, minimum wage negotiations and oth...
item.content:encoded:
The Federal Government has approved a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants for six months, beginning in November 2026, as part of measures to cushion the impact of rising living costs.

The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a conciliation meeting between the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress in Abuja on October 27, 2026.

The agreement also covers outstanding allowances, health workers’ arrears, minimum wage negotiations and other welfare issues.

Here are 10 key things to know about the transport allowance and other resolutions.

1. The allowance is N70,000 monthly

The Federal Government has approved N70,000 per month as transport support for public servants. The memorandum states that the intervention will apply “across all levels”.

2. Payment begins in November 2026

The allowance is scheduled to commence in November 2026. However, the memorandum does not specify the exact payment date or whether disbursement will be made alongside workers’ salaries.

3. It will last for six months

The transport intervention is temporary and will run for six months, beginning in November 2026. This means the approved period runs through April 2027, subject to implementation of the agreement.

4. Eligible workers could receive N420,000 in total

At N70,000 monthly for six months, the total transport support amounts to N420,000 per beneficiary over the approved period.

This is the total for the six-month intervention, not a one-off payment of N420,000.

5. It is separate from the national minimum wage

The transport allowance is a distinct intervention and should not be confused with the national minimum wage.

Although the statutory minimum wage was increased from N30,000 to N70,000 in 2024, the latest meeting did not resolve the disagreement over the effective date of implementing the minimum wage arrangements currently under discussion.

The government and labour leaders agreed to establish a Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee and begin meetings immediately.

6. The payment arrangements are yet to be clarified

Although the memorandum confirms the amount, duration and commencement month, it does not explain the administrative process for payment.

It also does not specify whether workers must apply, the payment channel or the precise categories of public servants covered. Further clarification from the relevant authorities would be needed on these details.

7. State and local government workers are being encouraged to benefit

The memorandum urges state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and calls on unions to push for implementation.

However, the document does not establish that every state and local government has already approved payment. Workers outside the Federal Government service should therefore seek clarification from their respective authorities.

8. Outstanding peculiar allowance arrears will also be paid

The government approved the payment of outstanding peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026.

Payment is scheduled to begin in November 2026 and will be made in three equal monthly instalments. The memorandum does not disclose the total arrears or the amount individual beneficiaries will receive.

9. Health workers have a separate allowance arrangement

The government agreed to clear 19 months of outstanding allowances for health workers within three months, beginning in December 2026.

The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission is also expected to complete an assessment of the cost implications of adjusting the Consolidated Health Salary Structure within three weeks. A final decision on the adjustment has not yet been announced.

10. Other workers’ welfare issues remain unresolved

The agreement also addresses hazard allowances for agricultural officers and proposed tax relief for workers.

The agricultural officers’ beneficiaries and associated costs are undergoing verification, which is expected to be completed within two weeks. The tax relief proposal will be referred to the National Executive Council for consideration.

The government and the NLC are expected to reconvene after one month to review implementation of the resolutions.

What this means for public servants

The N70,000 monthly transport support is a six-month intervention intended to provide temporary financial relief. However, questions about the precise categories of eligible workers, payment arrangements and implementation by state and local governments remain open.

The extent of the relief workers receive will therefore depend on the implementation of the agreement and further administrative clarification.

item.title: Ogun 2027: Hunye Takes Governorship Battle To Obasanjo, Awaits Court Verdict - Politics
item.description:

According to a statement issued by the Abayomi Hunye Media Team, the meeting focused on Hunye’s governorship ambition, the ongoing court proceedings and broader issues concerning le...
item.content:encoded:
The 2027 governorship battle in Ogun State has taken another political turn as governorship aspirant Abayomi Hunye held a private meeting with former President Olusegun Obasanjo, amid his continuing legal challenge over the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship nomination process.

According to a statement issued by the Abayomi Hunye Media Team, the meeting focused on Hunye’s governorship ambition, the ongoing court proceedings and broader issues concerning leadership, governance, political stability and the democratic process in Ogun State.

The development comes against the backdrop of a lingering dispute over the APC governorship primary, which produced Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, as the party’s recognised candidate. Hunye has continued to challenge aspects of the process in court.

Hunye has maintained that the matter should be determined strictly through the judicial process and has expressed confidence that the courts will examine the issues on their merits.
His latest engagement with Obasanjo is therefore being viewed by his camp as part of broader consultations with experienced statesmen as the 2027 political contest gathers momentum.

However, the meeting itself should not be interpreted as an endorsement of Hunye’s aspiration by the former president, as no such endorsement was stated in the announcement.

The legal battle remains a significant component of the unfolding Ogun APC crisis. Hunye has previously challenged the circumstances surrounding the party’s nomination process and, more recently, instituted legal proceedings seeking judicial examination of electoral documents previously submitted by Adeola.

Meanwhile, the APC has publicly maintained that Adeola remains its recognised governorship candidate for the 2027 election, while Hunye insists that the issues before the courts should be allowed to run their course.

With political consultations intensifying ahead of 2027, the Hunye-Obasanjo meeting adds another layer to an already closely watched governorship contest in Ogun State.

The courts, rather than political declarations, will ultimately determine the legal issues presently before them.

APC Youth Leadership: Mummy Boys Vs City Boy Movement Power Tussle by Racoon(op): 8:53am
Since yesterday details have begun to fly around from the secret meeting held with a minister whose name was not mentioned; The meeting, which ran until late night Monday, 26th October 2026, was alleged to have been convened on the instructions of a stateman.

The details available to our correspondence read part as narrated by a few of those who were at the meeting held in Abuja.

A source said, "We got a call to take any available flight and ensure we come to Abuja today. Even without provision for our air tickets, we were told our transport and accommodation logistics will be provided upon arrival. We are still in Abuja till now, we will leave immediately after the press conference tomorrow."

"In the meeting we met some big boys' names withheld, and the agenda is simple: they want to get rid of the National Youth Leader, as they said he has failed to hand over the youth wing structure to our leader, and we are not going to allow him to hold on to it. So therefore, we are meeting you so that as state and senatorial youth leaders we want you to pass a vote of no confidence in his leadership, and that will give them us the opportunity to press further for his removal.

"We are giving you 30 million as state youth leaders. Share it among yourselves every 3 weeks; this will keep coming until after the election, and 5 million to the Senatorial every three weeks as well for the period of the campaign, as we are resolved that no single campaign funds will be channelled through the office of the National Youth Leader to the party youth structure." He said.

Another source said, "We have been given some conditions before we can access the first 30 million and 5 million, respectively. The conditions are we must organise a press conference and collate signatures to pass a vote of no confidence in the leadership of Dayo Israel and call for his removal."

Also narrating his own side to our correspondence in confidence, a northern youth leader said, "We in the north don't betray Amanah, trust. For me and I know some of my colleagues too who will not take part in the said press conference or append our signatures to any letter passing a vote of no confidence in the leadership of our national youth leader, Dr Dayo Israel" he said.

Meanwhile, we shall continue to monitor the trends as they unfold. APC youth has a very large population and has continued to grow, as the last e-membership registrations organised by the party show youth takes a significant number in the party membership.

@Segalinks Reacts

I knew @dayoisrael as a teenager, and we have mutual friends who took up the Project Nigeria cause over 25 years ago. He is an intelligent gentleman but may have proven to be a negligent politician of recent. He may have made critical errors at the most sensitive time, but I would not advise railroading him just months before the election. There seems to be a deeper undercurrent of loyalty-based conflict in this matter.

In fairness, there is nothing Dayo is being castigated for that the City Boys are not also guilty of. His side of the story is important, even though this is an internal party matter that I believe the elders can resolve. When we see a politician in office not pulling their weight, we should take a deeper look. We may find that a lack of operational funds as likely root cause. I am not happy with Dayo no doubt, because I know he can do better.

The City Boy movement’s leadership, on the other hand, is mobilizing independently of the youth leader’s operations, which is bound to create conflicts and loyalty issues. So, the first opportunity to show signs of life in the space was taken by the youth leader, ostensibly to demonstrate accountability. But this proved insensitive to the plight of citizens encouraged to weather the storm under economic pressure.

We can’t pretend that politics doesn’t cost money or that mobilization doesn’t require certain incentives. Most of the politicians crying blue murder today are doing worse in the name of campaigns. But there is no excusing the excesses of these campaign hubs. They must be curbed, and politicians in the ruling party must show equal responsibility toward the country’s struggling citizens.

The best solution is intervention, not simply replacing an imperfect individual, who is only taking instructions, with someone else willing to submit to powers outside the party structure. This too will have internal political consequences. Let the elders intervene and guide the youth accordingly. This is the best position observers outside the party can take in the interest of national progress without prejudice. 🤷🏽‍♂️

TikTok User Raises Alarm Over Alleged Sexual Assault Incidents in Delta State

A Nigerian woman identified as Ogeneru Kewe has expressed frustration over alleged sexual assault incidents in Delta State, accusing authorities of failing to adequately protect women.

In a video shared on TikTok, Ogeneru referenced an incident allegedly involving the sexual assault of women in Ozoro a few months ago. She also claimed that a similar incident occurred in the Ekpan and Effurun areas last week.

According to her, some of the affected women have spoken publicly about their experiences but are yet to receive justice.

She criticised the Delta State governor and local government authorities, questioning whether sufficient action was being taken to protect women and address the reported incidents.

Ogeneru expressed concern about women's ability to travel safely within the state, saying the situation had affected her pride in identifying as an indigene of Delta State.

However, the allegations concerning the latest reported incident have not been independently verified. The details of any related investigations or legal proceedings also remain unclear.

The claims have renewed attention on the importance of women's safety, proper investigations into sexual violence allegations and access to justice for survivors.

Supporters Of Arab Israeli Party Celebrate Election Results In Nazareth (Photos) by God1000(op): 8:24am
Supporters of Israel's Joint List Arab party celebrated in Nazareth on Tuesday after exit polls indicated historic performance, with party head Yousef Jabareen declaring that they had sent far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir “home.”

A supporter of the Joint List was filmed waving a keffiyeh, a traditional Palestinian garment symbolising resilience, identity and heritage in the face of Israel’s repeated human rights abuse.

Exit polls from Israel’s main television channels projected that the two Arab political lists would win a combined 17–18 seats in the 120-member parliament, up from 10 in the 2022 election.

According to exit polls published by Channel 12, Ra’am and the Joint List were projected to win seven and 11 seats, respectively, The Jerusalem Post reported.

Israeli by citizenship and Palestinian by heritage, Arab Israelis make up a fifth of the population but historically have voted at lower rates than Jewish Israelis.

They face systemic discrimination in Israel and live under an apartheid system, according to Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch.

item.title: Akinwumi Adesina Tells Tinubu: "I Have A Duty To Serve Nigeria, And I Will" - Politics
item.description:
‘I have a duty to serve Nigeria, and I will’ - Adesina tells Tinubu pic.twitter.com/TcwlmxOrA6

— Premium Times (@PremiumTimesng) October 28, 2026

Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Akinwumi Adesina, has declared his readiness to serve Nigeria in any capacity, saying he has a duty a...
item.content:encoded:
‘I have a duty to serve Nigeria, and I will’ - Adesina tells Tinubu pic.twitter.com/TcwlmxOrA6

— Premium Times (@PremiumTimesng) October 28, 2026

Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Akinwumi Adesina, has declared his readiness to serve Nigeria in any capacity, saying he has a duty and responsibility to contribute to the country’s development.

Mr Adesina made the declaration on Tuesday after meeting President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, where he briefed the president on his 10-year tenure at the continental development finance institution.

“I’m fully able to help Nigeria in any capacity. I’ve always had that. You know, my heart is always at home,” he told journalists after the meeting.

Asked what role he could play, Mr Adesina said he would help in any capacity the president considered appropriate, but stressed he was not seeking a government appointment.

“I’m not looking for a job. I’m not looking for anything. I’m just here to help. It’s my country. I have a duty, an obligation, and a responsibility to do so, and I will,” he said.

There was no announcement of a specific role or appointment for the former AfDB president following the meeting.

Mr Adesina, an agricultural economist, served as Nigeria’s minister of agriculture and rural development from 2011 to 2015 under former President Goodluck Jonathan before becoming the first Nigerian to lead the AfDB.

He was elected president of the bank in May 2015 and re-elected for a second five-year term in August 2020. His tenure ended in 2025.

As agriculture minister, he championed reforms to the distribution of subsidised farm inputs, including an electronic-wallet system that let farmers receive support for seeds and fertiliser via mobile phones.

The AfDB said the programme reached 15 million farmers within its first four years. The initiative was intended to improve access to agricultural inputs while reducing the role of intermediaries in their distribution.

At the AfDB, Mr Adesina oversaw the institution’s development agenda, which included expanding electricity access, improving food security, industrialising African economies, promoting regional integration and improving living standards.

During his leadership, the bank’s general capital increased from $93 billion to $208 billion in 2019, following a decision by its shareholders, the largest capital increase in the institution’s history at the time.

AfDB provided $7 billion to Nigeria in 10 years
At the meeting, Mr Adesina said the AfDB provided about $7 billion in financing to Nigeria between 2015 and 2025. He compared this with the $11.1 billion in cumulative financing the bank had provided to Nigeria since it began operations in the country in 1971.

“Within 10 years, we were able to do 63 per cent, literally, of that,” he said, adding that President Tinubu was pleased with the bank’s support to Nigeria during his tenure.

Mr Adesina said he used the meeting to commend the president for his economic reforms, particularly the removal of the petrol subsidy and the harmonisation of the foreign exchange windows. He described the measures as difficult but said they were beginning to produce results.

He cited increased foreign exchange availability, the return of portfolio investors and a downward trend in inflation as signs of progress. However, he acknowledged that prices remained high for Nigerians

He also pointed to improved assessments of Nigeria by some international rating agencies, saying the country’s outlook had shifted towards stable or positive assessments.

The comments come amid ongoing debate over the impact of the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, including higher fuel costs after the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange market.

Although the government has defended the measures as necessary to stabilise the economy, the higher cost of living has continued to put pressure on households and businesses.

From economic stabilisation to growth
Mr Adesina said stabilising the economy was only the beginning, arguing that Nigeria must now focus on structural transformation, economic growth and prosperity.

He said President Tinubu recognised the need to move beyond macroeconomic reforms and address the broader challenge of transforming the economy.

"I told the president, I’m back at home, here to help and ready to help. It’s my country. I love my country, and I’m ready to help,” he said.

His offer comes after a decade leading one of Africa’s major development finance institutions, a period during which the bank financed projects and programmes across sectors including agriculture, energy, transport and infrastructure.

Mr Adesina’s meeting with the president also gave him an opportunity to formally brief the president on the completion of his two terms and the achievements recorded during his leadership of the bank.He said he was honoured to have been received by the president and was pleased with the report he presented.

While Mr Adesina did not specify how he might contribute to Nigeria’s development, he said he was prepared to do so whenever the president believed his experience could be useful.

“It’s my country. I have a duty, an obligation, and a responsibility to do so, and I will,” he said.

item.content:encoded:
NRC Invites Private Firms To Run Own Trains On Its Tracks. by AnonPoet(op): 7:52am

NRC invites private firms to run own trains on its tracks.

The Nigerian Railway Corporation (NRC), established for sole control of railways, is offering private operators access to its approximately 4,000.

The Nigerian Railway Corporation (NRC), established for sole control of railways, is offering private operators access to its approximately 4,000 km rail network for a fee, provided they supply their own locomotives and rolling stock.

Kayode Opeifa, managing director of the NRC, said the corporation grants what it calls track access, permitting private and private companies to operate on railway infrastructure built with public funds.

“You can bring your train, bring your locomotive, bring your wagons, bring your everything. We will run it on it. You just pay us your money. We don’t want to run the trains alone,” Opeifa told stakeholders Tuesday

Source
