item.title: Chris Brown Gets Eight-Month Suspended Sentence Over London Nightclub Fight - Celebrities
item.description:
American R&B singer Chris Brown has avoided immediate imprisonment after a London court sentenced him to eight months in prison, suspended for 12 months, over an attack on a music producer at a nightclub in 2023.

The 37-year-old singer was sentenced on Monday, October 26, 2026, at Southwark Crown Court after pleading guilty to affray over the incident at Tape nightclub in Mayfair, London, in the early hours of February 19, 2023.

Brown’s vocal coach and fell...
item.content:encoded:
American R&B singer Chris Brown has avoided immediate imprisonment after a London court sentenced him to eight months in prison, suspended for 12 months, over an attack on a music producer at a nightclub in 2023.

The 37-year-old singer was sentenced on Monday, October 26, 2026, at Southwark Crown Court after pleading guilty to affray over the incident at Tape nightclub in Mayfair, London, in the early hours of February 19, 2023.

Brown’s vocal coach and fellow rapper, Omololu Akinlolu, who also participated in the attack, received a four-month prison sentence, suspended for 12 months.

Both men were ordered to pay £1,500 in costs.

The case involved an attack on music producer Abraham ‘Abe’ Diaw, who sustained injuries after Brown struck him with a glass tequila bottle during the incident.

During the sentencing hearing, the court watched CCTV footage showing Brown hitting Diaw four times with the bottle, with two blows connecting with his head. The footage also showed the singer striking the victim’s shoulder.

Prosecutor Heidi Stonecliffe KC told the court that Brown approached Diaw on the dance floor at about 3:00 a.m. and attacked him with a heavy, square-shaped tequila bottle.

The prosecution further stated that Akinlolu joined the assault by punching Diaw in the head. The attack reportedly continued as the victim attempted to escape through the nightclub, with the court hearing that he was also kicked while sitting defenceless on the floor.

The incident lasted between 17 and 20 seconds, according to the defence.

Judge Describes Attack As Dangerous

While delivering his judgment, Judge Tony Baumgartner described Brown’s actions as dangerous, warning that repeatedly striking someone on the head with a glass bottle could have resulted in more serious injuries.

He said the attack involved serious violence, even though it was not planned.

The judge also noted that Brown had to be physically pulled away from the victim during the incident.

According to the judge, violence in a crowded nightclub poses a danger not only to the person being attacked but also to other people in the vicinity.


He emphasised that Brown’s celebrity status, commercial success and professional achievements did not entitle him to special treatment under the law.

However, the court considered several factors before deciding against immediate imprisonment, including Brown’s guilty plea, his compliance with bail conditions and the potential effect of a prison sentence on his four children.

The judge also concluded that the singer presented a low risk of committing further offences.

Why Brown Was Not Sent To Prison

Despite describing the incident as serious enough to warrant custodial sentences, Judge Baumgartner said recent changes to sentencing laws meant the prison terms had to be suspended unless exceptional circumstances justified immediate imprisonment.

The judge said he had considered whether the seriousness of the offences, together with the need for punishment and deterrence, justified sending the two men straight to prison.

He concluded that the circumstances did not meet the threshold for making an exception to the new legal requirement.

As a result, Brown and Akinlolu will not serve their prison sentences unless the terms of their suspension are breached in a way that leads to activation of the sentences.

Victim Received Hospital Treatment
Following the attack, Diaw was taken to St Mary’s Hospital in London for medical treatment.

The court heard that he was discharged with pain relief after being diagnosed with a head injury and a superficial knee injury.

An MRI scan conducted in early March reportedly revealed a high-grade injury to a ligament on the inner side of his left knee.

However, Brown’s defence lawyer, Sallie Bennett-Jenkins KC, disputed the extent of the injuries, arguing that the incident did not result in fractures or broken skin.

The defence described the attack as a brief incident that Brown deeply regretted.

Bennett-Jenkins told the court that the singer apologised to those who witnessed the incident and acknowledged the distress it may have caused.


The court also heard that Diaw was no longer supportive of the prosecution and had withdrawn his support some time after the incident.

Brown Had Faced More Serious Charges

Brown and Akinlolu pleaded guilty to affray at Southwark Crown Court in July 2026.

The singer had initially been scheduled to stand trial over more serious allegations, including assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm and possession of an offensive weapon. Those charges were subsequently dropped.

Akinlolu’s lawyer, Laurie-Anne Power KC, told the court that her client genuinely believed Brown was under attack when he intervened.

She described the relationship between the two men as close, saying Akinlolu regarded Brown as a brother. However, he accepted responsibility for his involvement in the incident.

Cheers As Chris Brown Leaves Court
After the sentencing, Brown and Akinlolu stood facing each other and clasped hands before leaving the courtroom.

Brown was greeted by loud cheers from supporters outside the court. He also appeared to stop to sign an autograph before departing.

item.title: World Leaders React As Lula Wins Fourth Term As Brazil’s President - Foreign Affairs
item.description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has secured a historic fourth non-consecutive term in office after defeating right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the country’s presidential run-off election.

Lula’s victory has attracted reactions from political leaders across the world, with several presidents and politicians congratulating him and expressing hope for stronger diplomatic relations, economic cooperation and democratic governance.

The election result, an...
item.content:encoded:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has secured a historic fourth non-consecutive term in office after defeating right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the country’s presidential run-off election.

Lula’s victory has attracted reactions from political leaders across the world, with several presidents and politicians congratulating him and expressing hope for stronger diplomatic relations, economic cooperation and democratic governance.

The election result, announced on Sunday, October 25, 2026, was celebrated by Lula’s supporters, who flooded the streets to mark his return to power.

However, Flávio Bolsonaro has called for the election to be annulled, describing a two-hour extension of voting time as unacceptable. The extension was granted by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin, although both presidential candidates had reportedly requested additional time for voting.

The dispute has sparked criticism from some conservative figures in the United States, while several progressive politicians have praised the outcome as a victory for democracy.

World Leaders Congratulate Lula
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum congratulated Lula in a message posted on X, declaring that democracy had prevailed and that the Brazilian people had won.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also congratulated the Brazilian president, expressing optimism about strengthening relations between Canada and Brazil.

Carney said both countries should seize the opportunity to expand trade, create new business opportunities, protect the environment and improve prosperity for their citizens.

Reactions From The United States
Reactions in the United States were divided, with conservative and progressive politicians expressing contrasting views about Lula’s victory.

Donald Trump Jr., son of US President Donald Trump, criticised the election process, focusing on the two-hour extension of voting time. He argued that the American mainstream media would have reacted differently if a conservative government had been involved in a similar situation.

Meanwhile, progressive Senator Bernie Sanders congratulated Lula on what he described as an extraordinary re-election victory.

Sanders praised the Brazilian president for standing up for workers and democracy, adding that he expected Lula to continue doing so during his next four years in office.

US Congressman Ro Khanna also welcomed the result, describing it as part of a wider global resistance against extremism. He argued that authoritarian leaders often attack democratic institutions because they fear the will of the people.

Khanna further urged President Donald Trump to respect the election outcome and avoid undermining Brazil’s electoral process.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani also celebrated Lula’s victory, sharing a message emphasising unity among the people.

California Governor Gavin Newsom’s media office equally expressed support for Brazil, highlighting shared commitments to democracy, environmental protection, workers’ rights and building an economy that benefits working families.

China And Russia Welcome Lula’s Victory
China congratulated Lula through Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun, who said Beijing respected the announcement by Brazil’s electoral authorities that the president had won the second round of voting.

Guo added that China was willing to work with Brazil to strengthen bilateral cooperation and advance their shared development objectives.

Russia also welcomed Lula’s re-election, with Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov praising his contributions to relations between the two countries and to the development of the BRICS organisation.

Peskov expressed hope that cooperation between Moscow and Brasília would continue to grow under Lula’s new administration.

Latin American Leaders Express Support
Several Latin American leaders also congratulated Lula, expressing optimism about stronger regional cooperation and closer diplomatic relations.

Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel described Lula’s victory as historic, saying it would sustain Brazil’s commitment to peace, national sovereignty and social justice.

He also expressed Cuba’s readiness to work with Brazil towards greater unity and integration across Latin America and the Caribbean.

Chilean President José Antonio Kast said he had spoken with Lula by telephone to congratulate him. Kast noted that both countries had opportunities to strengthen economic cooperation and work together to combat organised crime in the region.

Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori reaffirmed her country’s commitment to strengthening its strategic partnership with Brazil, particularly in regional integration, cooperation and the sustainable development of the Amazon, which both countries share.

Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz described Brazil and Bolivia as neighbouring countries with a shared history and common challenges. He said both nations would continue working together to strengthen relations and create more opportunities for their people.

Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino also congratulated the Brazilian people on the election and praised Lula’s victory, expressing his country’s commitment to continued cooperation with Brazil.

European Leaders Celebrate The Result
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen congratulated Lula, saying the outcome represented a victory for democracy and multilateralism.

She also highlighted the growing partnership between Europe and Brazil, pledging continued cooperation on free and open trade, international rules and climate action.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described Lula’s victory as a progressive comeback. He expressed hope that the Brazilian result would inspire similar political developments in Spain and other countries.

French President Emmanuel Macron called for stronger strategic relations between France and Brazil, saying both nations had significant opportunities to deepen their partnership and contribute to a fairer world.

Other Leaders Congratulate Lula
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa congratulated Lula, noting that countries in the region shared common challenges and stood to benefit from closer cooperation.

Paraguayan President Santiago Peña praised the Brazilian people for their democratic participation and said Brazil and Paraguay would continue working together on regional integration and development.

Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi also congratulated Lula after speaking with him, describing the election as an important democratic celebration.

Former Argentine President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner congratulated the Brazilian people and Lula, praising his ability to mobilise supporters and secure victory in the closely watched contest.

Lula Faces Expectations Ahead Of His New Term
Lula’s victory marks a significant development in Brazilian politics, with reactions from governments and politicians reflecting both support for his leadership and continuing divisions over the country’s political direction.

While several international leaders have expressed confidence in stronger economic, environmental and diplomatic cooperation with Brazil, the challenge to the election result by Flávio Bolsonaro has added controversy to the outcome.

As Lula prepares for another four-year term, attention is expected to focus on his ability to deliver on domestic promises, strengthen Brazil’s international partnerships and address concerns surrounding democracy and political ddivisions

item.title: Nigerian Refineries Receive 127 Million Barrels Of Crude Oil In Nine Months - Business
item.description:
Domestic refineries in Nigeria received more than 127 million barrels of crude oil and condensate between January and September 2026, according to the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC).

The development reflects improvements in the implementation of the Domestic Crude Supply Obligation (DCSO), which requires oil producers to prioritise local refineries in crude oil supply.

The Commission Chief Executive, Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this...
item.content:encoded:
Domestic refineries in Nigeria received more than 127 million barrels of crude oil and condensate between January and September 2026, according to the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC).

The development reflects improvements in the implementation of the Domestic Crude Supply Obligation (DCSO), which requires oil producers to prioritise local refineries in crude oil supply.

The Commission Chief Executive, Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this on Monday, October 26, 2026, while delivering a speech at the OTL Africa Downstream Energy Week 2026 in Lagos.

Eyesan, who was represented by the Assistant Director of Operations, Mr. Prosper Omonedo, said the commission had taken steps to improve crude oil deliveries following disagreements between oil producers and refinery operators that disrupted supplies in the first quarter of the year.

According to her, engagements between the commission, producers and refiners helped improve deliveries in the second and third quarters.

She explained that domestic refineries received 53.7 million barrels of crude oil and condensate in the second quarter, representing 97.4 per cent performance, while 45.1 million barrels were supplied in the third quarter, representing 76.2 per cent performance.

“From Q1–Q3 of 2026, more than 127 million barrels of Nigerian crude went to Nigerian refineries,” she stated.

Under Section 109 of the Petroleum Industry Act 2021, the NUPRC is responsible for ensuring that domestic refineries receive crude oil supplies before producers export their products.

The commission said it was continuing to engage stakeholders to address supply challenges and improve the availability of crude oil for local refining.

NUPRC Plans Crude Oil Swap Framework
Eyesan also disclosed that the commission was consulting oil producers, refiners and other stakeholders on a proposed domestic crude oil swap framework aimed at reducing transportation costs and improving supply efficiency.

Under the proposed arrangement, refinery operators could receive crude oil from the nearest suitable production or export terminal instead of transporting an allocated crude grade over long distances.

According to the commission, the arrangement could reduce transportation costs by an estimated $3 to $4 per barrel, potentially lowering refining expenses and improving the competitiveness of locally refined petroleum products.

The framework is expected to address some of the logistical challenges affecting crude oil deliveries to domestic refineries.

Nigeria’s Oil Production Records Improvement
On crude oil production, Eyesan said Nigeria recorded an average output of 1.717 million barrels per day of crude oil and condensate in September 2026.

This represented a 2.34 per cent increase compared with the previous month.

She added that crude oil production alone averaged 1.53 million barrels per day, marking the fifth consecutive month the industry met or exceeded its production quota.

The NUPRC chief attributed the improvement to better maintenance of oil production facilities, enhanced security around crude oil transportation infrastructure, stronger cooperation with operators and sustained regulatory efforts to restore previously shut-in production.

She said the commission would continue working with industry operators to sustain the production gains and strengthen Nigeria’s position in the global oil market.Buy Maps

NUPRC Promises Transparent Licensing Round
Speaking on the 2026 oil licensing round, Eyesan said the 40 oil blocks being offered to investors would undergo a transparent evaluation process.

She explained that the commission had established published evaluation criteria and mandatory disclosure of beneficial ownership to promote accountability and discourage the misuse of oil licences.

The NUPRC also reaffirmed its commitment to enforcing the drill-or-drop principle, which is designed to discourage companies from holding oil licences for speculative purposes without developing the assets.

Under the principle, licence holders are expected to carry out the required exploration and development activities within the stipulated period or risk losing their licences.

Eyesan noted that 22 recent awardees were expected to contribute at least 250,000 barrels per day to Nigeria’s oil production within five years.

The commission said the licensing process was part of broader efforts to attract investment, increase production and ensure that oil assets are developed for the country’s economic benefit.

Commission Reaffirms Commitment To Domestic Gas Supply

The NUPRC chief further reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to meeting the Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation and improving coordination across Nigeria’s petroleum industry.

She said the commission would continue working with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) to align refinery demand with crude oil supply planning.

According to her, effective coordination between upstream producers, refinery operators and regulatory agencies would help ensure that improvements in oil production translate into tangible benefits for households, businesses and electricity generation.

The commission maintained that strengthening domestic crude supply, reducing transportation costs and increasing production would support the development of Nigeria’s refining industry and improve energy security.Buy Maps

The latest figures come amid ongoing efforts to expand local refining capacity, reduce dependence on imported petroleum products and ensure that a greater share of Nigeria’s crude oil resources supports domestic economic aactivities

China Defends Brands’ Withdrawal Of Sponsorship Deals With Mbappé by adenigga(op): 6:21am
The Chinese government has declared that the action taken against Kylian Mbappé by some major brands in China was in order.

A Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, stated Beijing's position on Tuesday after a video featuring the French football star circulated online.

"Any rhetoric or action that hurts the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be rejected across the sectors in China," Guo said.

A French talk show had asked Mbappé about his favourite meme of himself. "A video someone made of a guy; I think he was a Chinese dictator," he replied.

The clip, which triggered the controversy, shows a doctored image of Mbappé's face on the body of Mao Zedong, the founding leader of Communist China.

Dairy giant Mengniu, beverage maker Dongpeng, and cheese maker Milkground have all terminated their sponsorship agreements with Mbappé.

The Real Madrid star apologised in a statement on Tuesday, saying he now understands that his "ill-judged" comment hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities worldwide.

"I apologise to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention," Mbappé wrote. "I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry."

Source: https://dailypost.ng/2026/10/27/china-defends-brands-withdrawal-of-sponsorship-deals-with-mbappe/

item.title: Is Owning A Car Really A Liability? - Car Talk
item.description:
Funny how with AI being ubiquitous these days, many choose to remain ignorant. Poor education is a bad thing.

Rapmoney:
I find it really amusing when people say car is a luxury and liability. To be sincere, I see it as a way backward thinking. It clearly shows that the damage that a bad economy can cause to the brains of citizens and their way of reasoning is beyond what many of us can imagine....
item.content:encoded:
Funny how with AI being ubiquitous these days, many choose to remain ignorant. Poor education is a bad thing.

Rapmoney:
I find it really amusing when people say car is a luxury and liability. To be sincere, I see it as a way backward thinking. It clearly shows that the damage that a bad economy can cause to the brains of citizens and their way of reasoning is beyond what many of us can imagine.

It is only in this part of the world that people see car as luxury, and owning one is often seen as owning a liability. Let me tell you today for free, owning a car is owning an asset. In case you still do not understand it, A CAR IS AN ASSET AND NOT A LIABILITY.

Many Nigerians have always seen car as liability even when a litre of fuel was N47.

Benefits of Owning a Car

1. Comfort: A private car gives you comfort and makes you avoid the unnecessary troubles of Nigerian commuters. Many people are sad and depressed. Some are frustrated. They don't mind quarrelling with you over space inside keke or bus. Others don't mind keeping their loads on your legs just to inconvenience you inside a bus or Keke.

2. Ease of movement: There are type of places you stay, and you will understand the importance of owning a car. The distance of your house to the main road is something else. Bikes and Keke do not go inside because they fear coming out without carrying any passenger, and that is a huge lose on their part. Think of a situation where it rains or you are carrying something heavy or fragile. You go cry nwii for Nnewi.

3. Time management: Owning a car can make you manage your time better. The way passengers and drivers quarrel, argue, and fight over time wastage in loading passengers, inaccurate issuance of change, and other issues due to the high level of frustration in the country is on another level. The issue of pick and drop can take a chunk of your time and make you late for a meeting, an appointment or work.

4. Provision of comfort for your family: Taking your kids to school is easier when you own a car. This also extends to family outings when you would need to take your wife and kids to an entertainment spot for relaxation. Just imagine the whole family squeezing themselves inside a Keke or dragging space with strangers inside bus. Na lack of money make poor man say beer dey bitter.

5. You can earn with your car: Some people use their car as a means of making money through car hailing services like Bolt, etc. I have seen folks use such to rake in good money every month.

Final Note

Just buy a car that you can easily maintain. The ones that have parts readily available in the market. I recommend Toyota products. Nor go buy car wey your power nor reach just to prove that you have arrived. Do not purchase a car that is unique and uncommon because you want to be the only one in town driving such. Na unique and uncommon problems dey wait you too.

If you are citing maintenance as reason not to buy a car, you may die without buying one. Nor be only car dem dey maintain. You also maintain house, wife, children, and even girlfriend.

I am Rapmoney aka WarriParrot

Cc: Seun Mynd44 Lalasticlala Nlfpmod OAM4J Dominique Fergie001

item.title: Lagos Assembly Okays State Police, Demands Clear Power-Sharing - Politics
item.description:
The Lagos State House of Assembly has backed the proposed establishment of state police but warned that the constitutional amendment before state legislatures must give states greater control over policing and clearly define the relationship between state and federal police authorities.

The Speaker, Mudashiru Obasa, raised the concerns on Tuesday during plenary after lawmakers considered the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2...
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State House of Assembly has backed the proposed establishment of state police but warned that the constitutional amendment before state legislatures must give states greater control over policing and clearly define the relationship between state and federal police authorities.

The Speaker, Mudashiru Obasa, raised the concerns on Tuesday during plenary after lawmakers considered the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, transmitted to state Houses of Assembly by the National Assembly.

Obasa said the proposed amendment was a significant step towards addressing Nigeria’s security challenges but argued that the provisions did not yet sufficiently resolve questions about who would control and administer state police.

“While the proposed amendment represents a step in the right direction, there is still room for improvement to ensure that future administrations can strengthen the provisions and grant states greater authority in managing their security systems,” he said.

The Speaker said the demand for state police had persisted through successive National Assemblies, from the fifth to the 10th, as governments continue to seek ways to improve security and protect lives and property.

He said the current proposal represented progress because the long-standing demand was finally receiving constitutional attention, but cautioned that leaving substantial powers at the federal level could undermine the purpose of creating state police.

Obasa also called for clear constitutional provisions defining the functions and responsibilities of the proposed state police, warning that differences in the powers assigned to federal and state authorities could create an imbalance in the country’s policing structure.

This comes as state Houses of Assembly consider the constitutional alteration required to establish a State Police Service, with nearly 25 states already expressing support for the proposal.

He commended President Bola Tinubu, the National Assembly leadership and state legislatures for pushing the amendment process, while urging lawmakers at all levels to ensure that the remaining concerns were addressed before the process was concluded.

Obasa used the debate to make a separate case for parliamentary policing, saying legislative institutions also required dedicated security arrangements to protect their independence.

He cited previous incidents in which state legislative complexes were allegedly demolished or locked at the instance of governors, arguing that parliamentary police could help prevent such occurrences and protect lawmakers from executive interference.

According to him, protecting legislative institutions was necessary to strengthen democratic governance and preserve the independence of the legislature.

“Protecting the legislature is essential to strengthening democratic institutions, preserving the independence of the legislative arm of government, and sustaining democracy in Nigeria,” he said.

Obasa directed the Clerk of the House, Adenike Oshinowo, to formally communicate the Lagos Assembly’s resolution to the National Assembly.

• T...
item.content:encoded:
Mr Thomas Hayes is the i9 Sports youth league director who called the Police during a viral dispute at the Martin Luther King Jr. Park in Winter Park, Florida.

The incident involved 3-year-old soccer prodigy Nevada Pierre, who was playing up in a league designed for 5-year-olds. The clash has sparked immense internet debate, with two entirely conflicting narratives surrounding why the police were ultimately called.

The Two Sides of the Dispute

• The Parents' Account:

The child's mother, Martasia Griffin, and father, Don Pierre, claim that their son was being unfairly targeted and kicked out of the league simply because he was "too good" at soccer. They shared videos online showing Nevada effortlessly dominating the pitch and scoring multiple goals, arguing that other parents grew frustrated because their children couldn't take the ball away from him. They felt the league was penalizing a toddler for his natural athletic talent.

• Thomas Hayes' Account (The League):

Hayes told dispatchers and responding officers that the call had nothing to do with the child's talent, which he openly admitted was "very advanced" and "great." Instead, Hayes stated that Nevada was repeatedly pushing and playing too aggressively with the other children. Because the recreational league prioritizes beginner fun and equal rotation,

Hayes tried to substitute the boy. According to Hayes, Nevada's parents became "really, really disruptive" and "unruly," followed him around, called him names, and created a large scene in front of other families.

The Resolution

The Police arrived at the scene and officially classified the incident as a civil matter. No one was arrested, ticketed, or formally forced to leave. The family left voluntarily after the game concluded, and the league issued them a refund.

The child's mother has since shared full unedited game clips on Instagram to challenge the league's claims of pushing, stating that her son was traumatised by the event. She noted that he will be moving to a youth training program run by former pro soccer player Eddie Johnson.

Listen to recording of Mr Thomas Hayes' call to the police:

item.content:encoded:
The Kwara State Police Command has arrested three suspected members of a kidnapping syndicate allegedly linked to multiple abductions in the state, including a man intercepted while wearing a hijab and carrying charms.

A team of Forest Guards led by Jebrin Adam arrested the suspect, identified as Aliyu Isiaka, at Okolowo, Ilorin, on October 24, 2026, at about 6 pm.

The arrest was disclosed in a statement issued on Tuesday by the command’s Police Public Relations Officer, Adetoun Ejire-Adeyemi, in Ilorin.

The statement said Isiaka, a resident of Ga’a-Kpapa village in Moro Local Government Area, was intercepted while disguised in female attire and carrying a polythene bag containing assorted charms.

“The suspect was intercepted while disguised in female attire, wearing a hijab and carrying a polythene bag containing assorted charms,” the statement read.

The police said the suspect confessed during interrogation to being a member of a nine-man kidnapping syndicate allegedly led by one Juli, who resides at Fulani Camp, Ga’a-Kpapa, and is currently at large.

According to the statement, Isiaka disclosed that he was recruited into the gang in August 2026 and had participated in three kidnapping operations at Oloru, Alapa and Malete, where substantial ransom payments were allegedly collected.

"Following further investigation and operational coordination, a joint team of police personnel and Forest Guards raided the suspected kidnappers’ camp on October 25, leading to the arrest of two additional male suspects identified as Seriki and Jebrin.

item.description:

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appeared to lose significant support to opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot in the Israeli election Tuesday, according to exit polls — but neither bloc was set to win enough seats to secure a clear majority.

The big story, however, was the huge gain for Israeli Arabs, who make up about 25% of the population....
item.content:encoded:
Netanyahu loses seats, trails challenger Gadi Eisenkot in Israel election, exit polls show — here’s what happens next

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appeared to lose significant support to opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot in the Israeli election Tuesday, according to exit polls — but neither bloc was set to win enough seats to secure a clear majority.

The big story, however, was the huge gain for Israeli Arabs, who make up about 25% of the population.

They were on pace to score 17 seats, a huge increase.

Netanyahu’s Likud party had 25 seats, and his right-wing alliance had 50, according to the Kan 11 exit poll published after voting ended. That would be a massive drop from the 32 they currently hold.

Israel election turnout on pace for highest in 50 years — as Gal Gadot casts her ballot

Despite the drop, the party is still projected to get the most votes out of any other single party in the election, according to all major exit polls.

Meanwhile, the “Change” opposition is slated to win 52 to 53 seats.

Opposition parties currently hold 50 seats in the 120-member Knesset.

“If these are the final results, they would mark a victory,” Eisenkot said in a statement.

“Netanyahu’s bloc suffered a tough defeat,” added Yari Lapid, a fellow opposition leader. “This is a total collapse and the public told them to go home.”

At least 38 parties were running for the Knesset, leaving the minor players — especially Israel’s Arab parties — in a position to decide the future of the country as both Netanyahu’s bloc and Eisenkot’s bloc jockey for a majority.

Israel election turnout on pace for highest in 50 years — as Gal Gadot casts her ballot

Ex-Netanyahu adviser lays out 3 big hurdles giving anti-Bibi camp the edge in heated Israeli election
Polls open in Israel for country’s first election since October 7 attacks

Both sides appeared to fall short of the 61 seats needed to elect a prime minister and form a government.

The Arab parties only held 10 seats in Knesset prior to the election, with Tuesday’s election seeing a high Arab-voter turnout compared to the 2022 election.

That could leave them as the kingmakers — if Eisenkot breaks a campaign promise and works with them.

“When you have Arabs at 17, you can’t disregard them,” Israeli journalist Attila Somfalvi said at the Israel Press Club’s election-night press center in Tel Aviv.

Retired Israeli Air Force Maj. Gen. Nimrod Sheffer, a candidate for the left-wing Democrats party that scored 9-10 seats in the exit polls, revealed on Tuesday that the anti-Netanyahu coalition had met with Arab leaders to discuss forming a new government together should the election results favor them.

It will take time to count the ballots as Israel officiates its elections the old fashioned way.

The official results will paint a clearer picture come Wednesday, but it could take as much as three weeks to a month for the winning parties to establish a coalition to set up a ruling government.

It will eventually fall on Israeli President Isaac Herzog to select a party leader he believes will win the majority of support in Knesset.

Herzog has three chances to tap a worthy candidate, but should the Knesset fail to rally around his pick, a new round of elections would be held.

Netanyahu will remain the country’s acting prime minister until a new premier is elected.

‘I'll act immediately to replace Netanyahu’: Eisenkot responds to Israel exit polls

Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar! party, vowed Tuesday night to act immediately to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government after Israel's election exit polls gave the bloc seeking political change a narrow advantage, although neither side secured the parliamentary majority needed to form a government.

"The initial results indicate a complete vote of no confidence in Netanyahu and the government of October 7 by the Zionist majority and the majority of Israeli citizens," Eisenkot said, referring to the government in office during the Hamas-led attack on Israel.

"If these are the final results, this is a victory for the mainstream Zionist majority in Israel," he added. "I will act immediately to implement the people's decision, replace Netanyahu's government and establish a Zionist government committed to military conscription as soon as possible."

The average of the exit polls published by Kan 11, Channels 12 and 13 gives the change bloc 53 seats, compared with 50 for Netanyahu's bloc. The Arab parties are projected to win a combined 17 seats, leaving neither of the two main political blocs with the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset.

Despite the narrow lead for Netanyahu's opponents, Likud is projected to remain Israel's largest individual party, setting the stage for potentially difficult coalition negotiations once the official results are known.

Eisenkot's Yashar! projected to win 19 to 23 seats
Eisenkot's Yashar! party is projected to win 21
seats in Kan 11's exit poll, 22 in Channel 12's and 23 in Channel 13's. The i24NEWS poll gives the party 20 seats, while Channel 14 projects 19.
Across all five exit polls, the former military chief's party averages 21 seats, placing it among the country's largest political factions, behind Likud.

Eisenkot, Israel's 21st IDF chief of staff, entered politics in 2022, three years after leaving military service. He joined Benny Gantz's National Unity alliance and was placed third on its electoral list.

item.content:encoded:
Peter Obi Raises Alarm Over Out-Of-School Children, Corruption In Nigeria by NationalFocusNG(op): 10:18pm On Oct 27
Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has identified corruption, education challenges and rising living costs as major problems confronting Nigeria.

Obi stated this on Tuesday during a town hall meeting in Lokoja, Kogi State, as part of his nationwide consultations.

He lamented that Nigeria still has the highest number of out-of-school children globally, despite the establishment of the historic Holy Trinity Primary School in Lokoja in 1865.

Obi also identified corruption as a major obstacle to national development, stressing the need to invest in education, healthcare, agriculture and local production to reduce poverty.

He further highlighted Kogi State's tourism potential and called attention to the need to preserve historical sites, including the Iron of Liberty monument.

The NDC presidential candidate also visited Kpata Market, where traders complained about rising prices of goods and declining patronage due to reduced consumer purchasing power.

item.content:encoded:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRiqv6wQ0m8

Popular Nigerian comedian and actor Ayo Makun, popularly known as AY, has apologised to fans following the disruption of his comedy show in Cardiff, Wales, United Kingdom.

The show, part of his “AY Live: Single and Not Searching” UK tour, was scheduled for Sunday, October 25, 2026. Reports indicated that audience members waited for hours but left disappointed after the expected performances did not take place.

In his response, AY said he and other comedians travelled to Cardiff and eventually entered the venue, but unresolved payment commitments delayed their appearance. According to him, most of the audience had already left by the time they arrived at the hall.

The entertainer expressed regret over the experience, acknowledging that ticket holders deserved better organisation and timely communication.

AY also called on the event organisers and UK tour management to provide a clear resolution for affected customers, including information about refunds. He urged the public to listen to his full explanation before reaching conclusions about the incident.

As of October 27, 2026, the cited reports had not established a confirmed refund process announced by the organisers.

Despite the disruption, AY said his remaining UK tour dates in Birmingham, London, and Manchester were still scheduled for October 30, October 31, and November 1, respectively.

The incident has renewed attention on the importance of proper event coordination, communication, and clear refund arrangements when live performances are disrupted.

item.content:encoded:
Singer Omah Lay has announced the postponement of his ongoing world tour due to a knee ligament injury.

The singer, whose real name is Stanley Omah Didia, made the announcement in a post shared on his X handle.

In the post which he addressed to his fans as “SPIRITS”, Omah Lay said he was heartbroken to share the news, noting that all dates for his ‘Clarity of Mind’ tour from October 30th onwards have been postponed.

“I’m heartbroken to share that due to a knee ligament injury, all CLARITY OF MIND TOUR dates from October 30th onwards are postponed as I focus on recovery over the next 4-6 weeks,” he wrote.

He added that rescheduled dates and ticket updates would be communicated later, while thanking his fans for their love.

The ‘Clarity of Mind’ tour, named after his second studio album released earlier this year, began on September 25 in Edmonton, Canada.

FG Approves ₦70,000 Monthly Transport Allowance For Workers by UDOKABESTLUV(op): 9:47pm On Oct 27
The Federal Government has approved a N70,000 monthly transport intervention for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, to cushion the impact of rising living costs.

The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a conciliation meeting between the Federal Government and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday, following renewed pressure from organised labour over the rising cost of living, workers’ welfare and outstanding agreements.

The government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November.

However, the meeting ended without an agreement on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage.

Both parties agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and commence meetings immediately to address the outstanding issue.

Source: https://leadership.ng/just-in-fg-approves-n70000-monthly-transport-allowance-for-workers/

item.title: Peter Obi’s 2023 Lagos Victory Not A Permanent Inheritance – APC - Politics
item.description:
The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has said Peter Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election does not guarantee a repeat performance in 2027 given President Bola Tinubu's stellar performance.

The party’s spokesman in Lagos State, Seye Oladejo, stated this while responding to a question on whether Obi, who is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election could replicate his victory in La...
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has said Peter Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election does not guarantee a repeat performance in 2027 given President Bola Tinubu's stellar performance.

The party’s spokesman in Lagos State, Seye Oladejo, stated this while responding to a question on whether Obi, who is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election could replicate his victory in Lagos in the 2027 presidential poll.

In the 2023 elections, Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes, while Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) came third with 75,750 votes, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Some of his supporters known as Obidients have promised he will win with a higher number in 2027.

However, Oladejo, in a chat with Daily Independent said the political circumstances surrounding the next election would be substantially different from those that shaped the 2023 contest.

He acknowledged the significance of Obi’s performance in Lagos but maintained that electoral victories did not translate into permanent ownership of voters.

“Peter Obi’s performance in Lagos in 2023 was significant, and the APC does not make the mistake of dismissing voters who chose differently. However, elections are not permanent inheritances. Voters reassess candidates, political platforms, performance and prevailing circumstances at every election,” he said.

According to him, the 2023 election was influenced by a combination of factors, including a strong youth-driven political movement, public dissatisfaction and enthusiasm surrounding the Labour Party’s presidential candidate.

He, however, argued that such political momentum did not necessarily translate into a sustainable electoral structure.

“The real test is whether that enthusiasm can be sustained, organised and translated into votes across wards, local governments and the wider electorate,” Oladejo said.

The APC spokesman said his party would campaign on the record of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, the rationale behind its reforms, its interventions and plans for the future.

He added that the APC would rely on its established grassroots structure, governance record and extensive political network in Lagos to strengthen its position ahead of the 2027 election.

Oladejo said the party would not take its supporters for granted or assume that previous electoral victories automatically guaranteed future success.

“We are not taking our voters for granted, and we will not assume that past victories automatically guarantee future ones,” he said.

He insisted that Obi’s victory in Lagos in 2023 should be viewed as an electoral outcome rather than a permanent transfer of the state's electorate to the Labour Party.

“Peter Obi’s victory in Lagos in 2023 was an electoral outcome, not a permanent transfer of ownership of Lagos voters. In 2027, the APC will make its case directly to the electorate and work towards a decisive victory for President Tinubu,” Oladejo said.

Davido, Kirk Franklin Set To Release ‘Hope In You’ by UDOKABESTLUV(op): 9:37pm On Oct 27
Nigerian Afrobeats star Davido has collaborated with American gospel singer Kirk Franklin on a new song titled Hope in You, scheduled for release on Friday, October 30, 2026.

The song will feature on Franklin’s forthcoming 14-track album, I Am What I Am, which blends gospel music with contemporary sounds.

The collaboration was previewed at an album listening event in Atlanta, United States, on October 12, where Davido reportedly performed a verse and joined the choir.

The project also features American musicians GloRilla, Jelly Roll and Tobe Nwigwe, bringing together artists from different musical backgrounds.

The collaboration marks a meeting of Afrobeats and contemporary gospel, with the two artists bringing their distinct musical styles to the project.

item.content:encoded:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has explained that its raid on Applewood Estate, Orchid Road, Lekki, Lagos State, was aimed at arresting suspected cybercrime operators accused of defrauding unsuspecting victims through gift cards, cryptocurrency transactions and international money transfers.

The commission said the operation followed surveillance and reconnaissance on the activities of the suspected fraudsters, who allegedly impersonated various individuals to obtain money from their victims.

The operation, conducted by operatives of the EFCC’s Lagos Directorate 1 at about 5am on Monday, October 26, resulted in the arrest of 21 suspects and the recovery of five exotic cars.

In a statement on Tuesday, the EFCC’s head of media and publicity, Dele Oyewale said preliminary investigations had implicated 19 of the arrested suspects, while two others had been released.

He added that the 19 suspects who were indicted would be arraigned in court immediately.

The commission’s explanation comes amid questions surrounding the operation at the high-profile residential estate, with the agency insisting that the raid was based on intelligence gathering and was conducted professionally.

According to the EFCC, its operatives carried out pre-arrest surveillance to establish the activities of the suspects before moving in to apprehend them.

The agency said the suspected fraudsters allegedly used different methods, including gift cards, cryptocurrency and international money transfers, to obtain money from unsuspecting victims while impersonating other individuals.

The EFCC also addressed the circumstances surrounding the detention of a young woman during the operation.

Oyewale said the woman had attempted to alert the suspects by making telephone calls while the operation was ongoing. Her phone was temporarily confiscated until the operation was concluded but was subsequently returned to her, the commission said.

The agency maintained that the operation was conducted without harassment, intimidation or the unlawful arrest of anyone.

It also urged Nigerians to support efforts to combat economic and financial crimes, warning that cybercrime activities undermine the country’s reputation.

The commission said it remained open to constructive engagement with members of the public but would not allow what it described as blackmail and alarmism to frustrate its statutory responsibilities.
